en.topic: Writing in the style of an author

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does an author's 'style' mean?
options: The particular way an author uses words and sentences
The colour of the book cover
The number of pages in a book
questions.answer: The particular way an author uses words and sentences
questions.hint: Think about how the writing sounds, not what it looks like.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'I didn't want to go. Nobody asked me, of course.' Which narrative voice is this?
questions.hint: Look at the pronouns.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: An author often writes short sentences like 'Silence. Then a crack. Then nothing.' What effect does this usually create?
questions.hint: Think about how quickly you read it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence imitates a style that uses lots of sensory detail?
options: The salty wind stung my cheeks as gulls screamed overhead.
questions.answer: The salty wind stung my cheeks as gulls screamed overhead.
questions.hint: Look for touch, sound and taste.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: An author often begins chapters with a line of speech. Which opening imitates this?
options: It was a Tuesday in March.
Once upon a time there lived a farmer.
The village was small and quiet.
questions.hint: Look for inverted commas at the start.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Read: 'The old barn groaned, tired of standing in the storm.' Which technique is used?
questions.hint: The barn is given a human feeling.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: An author's narrator often speaks directly to the reader. Which sentence imitates this?
options: You might think I was brave. I wasn't.
questions.answer: You might think I was brave. I wasn't.
questions.hint: Look for 'you'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word best describes a narrator's voice that says: 'Honestly, who puts a pond right next to a football pitch?'
questions.hint: Imagine someone saying it with a smile.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: To imitate an author's sentence structure, what should you copy?
options: The pattern of the sentence, but with your own ideas and words
questions.answer: The pattern of the sentence, but with your own ideas and words
questions.hint: Imitating is not the same as copying out.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Model: 'Slowly, silently, the fox crept across the frozen field.' Which sentence follows the same structure?
options: Quickly, quietly, the girl slipped through the dark hallway.
The girl was quick and quiet.
A girl went into the hallway.
questions.answer: Quickly, quietly, the girl slipped through the dark hallway.
questions.hint: Look at how the model starts with two adverbs.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: An author often ends a chapter on a cliffhanger. Which ending is a cliffhanger?
options: Then the door handle began to turn.
We all went home and had tea.
And that was the end of the trip.
questions.answer: Then the door handle began to turn.
questions.hint: Which one makes you want to read on?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses the past tense and third person, like many adventure stories?
options: Lena climbed the wall and stared at the sea.
I climb the wall and stare at the sea.
questions.answer: Lena climbed the wall and stared at the sea.
questions.hint: Check the verb endings and the pronouns.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: An author's writing uses rich vocabulary about nature. Which word fits that style best in: 'The ___ hedgerow was full of blackbirds.'?
questions.hint: Choose the most precise, vivid word.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When writing a new chapter in an author's style, which of these is most important to keep the same?
questions.hint: Think about who is telling the story.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write two sentences that open a new chapter in the style of an author who uses short, tense sentences and a first-person narrator.
questions.hint: Use 'I' and keep your sentences short.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain one feature of an author's style that you would copy when writing a new chapter, and why it would make your chapter sound like theirs.
questions.hint: Think about voice, sentence length or vocabulary.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is technical vocabulary?
options: Words that belong to a particular subject, such as science
questions.answer: Words that belong to a particular subject, such as science
questions.hint: Think about words a scientist would use.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which feature is most typical of a scientific explanation text?
questions.hint: Explanation texts explain how or why something happens.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Plants make their own food through photosynthesis. Using energy from sunlight, they turn water and carbon dioxide into glucose, a type of sugar.' What is the technical word for how plants make their own food?
questions.hint: It is in the first sentence.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Plants make their own food through photosynthesis. Using energy from sunlight, they turn water and carbon dioxide into glucose, a type of sugar.' What does 'glucose' mean in this text?
questions.hint: The text explains it right after the comma.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Plants make their own food through photosynthesis. Using energy from sunlight, they turn water and carbon dioxide into glucose, a type of sugar.' Which gas do plants use to make glucose?
questions.hint: Look for the two things plants turn into glucose.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Your heart pumps blood around your body through tubes called blood vessels. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry it back.' What are blood vessels?
questions.hint: The text defines them using 'called'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Your heart pumps blood around your body through tubes called blood vessels. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry it back.' Which blood vessels carry blood back to the heart?
questions.hint: Look at the word 'while'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Your heart pumps blood around your body through tubes called blood vessels. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins carry it back.' Which word in the text signals a contrast between arteries and veins?
questions.hint: Which word shows two things are different?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Erosion is the process by which rock and soil are slowly worn away and moved by wind, water or ice. Over many years, rivers can carve deep valleys.' Using the context, what does 'erosion' mean?
options: Rock and soil being worn away and moved
Rock being made in a volcano
questions.answer: Rock and soil being worn away and moved
questions.hint: The text gives the definition after 'is'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Erosion is the process by which rock and soil are slowly worn away and moved by wind, water or ice. Over many years, rivers can carve deep valleys.' Which of these is NOT given as a cause of erosion?
questions.hint: Check the list in the first sentence.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'Erosion is the process by which rock and soil are slowly worn away and moved by wind, water or ice. Over many years, rivers can carve deep valleys.' Which sentence gives the main idea of the text?
options: Wind, water and ice slowly wear away and move rock and soil.
Soil is a type of rock.
questions.answer: Wind, water and ice slowly wear away and move rock and soil.
questions.hint: Which choice covers the whole text, not one detail?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'A circuit is a complete path that electricity can flow around. If there is a gap, the circuit is broken and the bulb will not light. Materials that let electricity pass through, such as copper, are called conductors.' What is a 'conductor'?
options: A material that lets electricity pass through
questions.answer: A material that lets electricity pass through
questions.hint: Find the sentence with 'are called'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'A circuit is a complete path that electricity can flow around. If there is a gap, the circuit is broken and the bulb will not light. Materials that let electricity pass through, such as copper, are called conductors.' Why would the bulb not light?
options: Because there is a gap and the circuit is broken
questions.answer: Because there is a gap and the circuit is broken
questions.hint: Look for the word 'if'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: In a scientific text, you meet the word 'transparent' next to the phrase 'lets light pass through, like glass'. What does this tell you about how texts help with technical words?
options: Writers often explain a technical word with a definition or example nearby
You must always use a dictionary
questions.answer: Writers often explain a technical word with a definition or example nearby
questions.hint: Look around the word for clues.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Read: 'A circuit is a complete path that electricity can flow around. If there is a gap, the circuit is broken and the bulb will not light. Materials that let electricity pass through, such as copper, are called conductors.' Explain in your own words what a circuit is and what happens when it is broken.
questions.hint: Use the words 'path' and 'gap'.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Give two strategies a reader can use to work out an unfamiliar technical word in a science text.
questions.hint: Think about context, word parts and glossaries.

en_spell.topic: Suffix -ly: -ally and changes to the root

questions.subject: en_spell

questions.hint: Words ending in -ic add a longer ending.

questions.hint: frantic ends in -ic.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Make an adverb from 'dramatic' and write the whole word.
questions.hint: Add the ending used for -ic words.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word is the exception to the -ic → -ally rule?
questions.hint: Which one only adds -ly?

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Choose the correct spelling: The results were announced ___.
questions.hint: This word is an exception.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the adverb from 'true'?
questions.hint: The e is dropped.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: who_ _y (meaning 'completely').
questions.hint: It comes from 'whole'; the e is dropped.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of the adverb from 'full'?
questions.hint: You don't need three l's.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which sentence is spelled correctly?
options: She smiled gently and spoke truly.
She smiled gentley and spoke truely.
She smiled gentlely and spoke truly.
She smiled gently and spoke truely.
questions.answer: She smiled gently and spoke truly.
questions.hint: Check both adverbs.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Fill in the missing letters and write the whole word: dramatic_ _ _y
questions.hint: Count the letters in the ending used for -ic words.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: humbley → humbly; dramaticly → dramatically; gentley → gently; truely → truly; publically → publicly
questions.hint: Check the -le, -ic and -e rules, and remember the exception.
questions.text: The actor bowed humbley after the play. He had moved dramaticly across the stage and spoken gentley to the audience. Some people were truely amazed. Basically, everyone agreed the show was fully deserving of its prize, and the director thanked the cast publically.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: franticaly → frantically; simpley → simply; wholey → wholly; fullly → fully
questions.hint: Look closely at the endings of the adverbs.
questions.text: Our dog barked franticaly when the storm began. Mum simpley closed the curtains and held him gently. The thunder was wholey terrifying for him. By morning he was fullly calm again and basically back to his usual self, wagging his tail dramatically.

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Touching a hot pan and pulling your hand away before you even think about it is called a …

questions.q: Which of these is a fair-test variable to keep the same in a ruler-drop reaction test?

questions.subject: ipc
questions.q: Why do you think tiredness might make a person's reaction time slower? Give one reason.
questions.hint: Think about how well the brain works when you need sleep.

pt_leit.topic: Divulgação científica: termos técnicos e explicações

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'A fotossíntese é o processo em que as plantas usam a luz do Sol para produzir seu próprio alimento.' O que é fotossíntese?
options: O jeito de as plantas produzirem alimento com luz
questions.answer: O jeito de as plantas produzirem alimento com luz
questions.hint: A explicação vem logo depois de 'é'.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Um texto de divulgação científica serve principalmente para…
options: explicar conhecimentos da ciência de forma acessível
questions.answer: explicar conhecimentos da ciência de forma acessível
questions.hint: Pense em quem é o público: pessoas curiosas, não cientistas.

questions.hint: Observe a palavra 'como' ligando duas coisas diferentes.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Qual destas expressões costuma introduzir uma explicação?
questions.hint: Ela anuncia que algo vai ser dito de outro jeito.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'Os animais herbívoros, isto é, que se alimentam de plantas, têm dentes largos.' O que significa 'herbívoros'?

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'A erosão — o desgaste do solo pela água e pelo vento — pode formar vales.' Para que servem os travessões?
questions.hint: Veja o que está entre os dois travessões.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'Os fósseis são restos ou marcas de seres vivos preservados em rochas.' Qual é o termo técnico definido nessa frase?
questions.hint: É a palavra que a frase explica.

questions.subject: pt_leit

questions.subject: pt_leit

O Sol gira em torno da Lua

questions.hint: Junte o termo técnico e sua explicação.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'Os anfíbios, como sapos e rãs, vivem parte da vida na água e parte na terra.' Qual informação o exemplo acrescenta?
options: Diz o que os sapos comem
questions.hint: Para que servem exemplos em uma explicação?

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'A água evapora, ou seja, passa do estado líquido para o gasoso.' Para qual estado a água passa quando evapora?
questions.hint: Procure a explicação depois de 'ou seja'.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'Os glóbulos brancos defendem o corpo contra micróbios, como soldados protegendo um castelo.' Nessa comparação, o castelo representa…
questions.hint: O que os 'soldados' estão protegendo?

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Leia: 'As abelhas fazem a polinização: levam o pólen de uma flor a outra, ajudando as plantas a produzir frutos.' Explique com suas palavras o que é polinização.
questions.hint: Use a explicação depois dos dois-pontos.

questions.subject: pt_leit
questions.q: Por que você acha que é importante explicar os termos técnicos em um texto para crianças?
questions.hint: Pense em como seria ler uma palavra que você nunca viu.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Qual palavra completa a frase? O preso ficou na ___ da delegacia.
questions.hint: Uma é um quartinho fechado; a outra vai no cavalo.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Qual palavra completa a frase? O vaqueiro colocou a ___ no cavalo.
questions.hint: Pense no assento do cavaleiro.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: O IBGE faz o ___ para contar a população do Brasil.
questions.hint: Uma das palavras significa contagem; a outra, juízo.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Ele tem um ótimo ___ de humor.
questions.hint: Qual delas tem a ver com percepção e juízo?

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Por favor, ___ a luz da sala.
questions.hint: Uma significa ligar ou pôr fogo; a outra, subir.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: O balão começou a ___ ao céu.
questions.hint: Qual delas significa subir?

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Compramos ingressos para a ___ das oito no cinema.
questions.hint: É o tempo em que algo acontece, como um filme.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Os livros de ciências ficam na ___ infantil da biblioteca.
questions.hint: Uma delas significa parte ou divisão.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: A lei proíbe ___ animais silvestres.
questions.hint: Uma é perseguir animais; a outra é anular um direito.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: O juiz decidiu ___ o mandato do político.
questions.hint: Qual delas significa anular ou tirar um direito?

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Homônimos homófonos são palavras que…
options: têm o mesmo som, mas grafia e sentido diferentes
têm grafias iguais e sons diferentes
questions.answer: têm o mesmo som, mas grafia e sentido diferentes
questions.hint: 'Homo' = igual, 'fono' = som.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Escreva a palavra que significa 'parte, divisão de algo' e soa como 'sessão'.
questions.hint: Ela tem ç.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Escreva o homófono de 'cela' que significa o assento usado para montar a cavalo.
questions.hint: Começa com s.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Caça-erros: encontre e corrija as 5 palavras escritas errado.
questions.answer: cela → sela; ascender → acender; seção → sessão; senso → censo; cassar → caçar
questions.hint: Pense no sentido de cada palavra na frase, não só no som.
questions.text: No sítio do meu tio, ele colocou a cela no cavalo e foi ascender a fogueira perto do lago. Mais tarde fomos à cidade ver a seção de cinema das sete. Na volta, ele falou sobre o senso que conta a população e disse que é proibido cassar onças na mata.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Escreva uma frase com 'acender' e outra com 'ascender', mostrando a diferença de sentido.
questions.hint: Uma tem a ver com fogo ou luz; a outra, com subir.

questions.subject: pt_ort
questions.q: Caça-erros: encontre e corrija as 4 palavras escritas errado.
questions.answer: sessão → seção; acender → ascender; sela → cela; censo → senso
questions.hint: Leia cada frase e pergunte: essa palavra faz sentido aqui?
questions.text: Na biblioteca, procurei a sessão de esportes e achei um livro sobre balões que podem acender até as nuvens. Outro livro contava a história de um ladrão preso numa sela escura. Meu irmão, com seu bom censo, disse que cassar o direito de alguém exige um julgamento justo.
